thread.title: Apple's Earnings Were Strong, but the Weak Spots Are in the Spotlight After a Turbulent October

title: Apple's Earnings Were Strong, but the Weak Spots Are in the Spotlight After a Turbulent October
text:
Apple’s Earnings Were Strong, but the Weak Spots Are in the Spotlight After a Turbulent October By Updated Nov. 1, 2018 5:50 p.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Saeed Kahn/AFP/Getty Images Text size
If Facebook (FB) appeased some tech investors with an earnings report that sent its shares up late Tuesday and Wednesday, Apple (AAPL) renewed their angst on Thursday.
Apple announced fiscal-fourth-quarter earnings that eased past analyst estimates, but disappointing guidance dragged the stock down 5% in extended trading. (Apple shares are up 31% this year.) Now, the question is whether Apple’s quarter will contribute to tech’s recent malaise.
The company reported earnings per share of $2.91 on revenue of $62.9 billion, representing an upside of 41% and 20%, respectively, from a year ago. Analysts polled by FactSet forecast EPS of $2.78 on revenue of $61.46 billion. Apple reached a market value of $1 trillion on Thursday, propelled by the sustained success of the iPhone. WSJ's Spencer Jakab takes a look at how Apple got here. Photo illustration: Heather Seidel/The Wall Street Journal
However, Apple’s guidance for fiscal-first-quarter revenue was $89 billion to $93 billion, while analysts projected $93.02 billion.
“We’re thrilled to report another record-breaking quarter that caps a tremendous fiscal 2018,” Apple CEO Tim Cook said in a statement, preceding a conference call with analysts. “We enter the holiday season with our strongest lineup of products and services ever.”
Apple also came up short in shipments. It sold 46.9 million iPhones in the quarter, about the same as a year ago. (Analysts expected 47 million.) More important, the average sales price per iPhone user was $793, versus the $729 expected by analysts .
Apple’s powerhouse Services division racked up a record $9.98 billion in revenue, up 27% from a year ago.
The September quarter is usually a transitional one for Apple, a prelude to its gargantuan holiday sales. It typically introduces new iPhones early in the month–as it did this year with iPhone XS Max, iPhone XS and iPhone XR–and sales of those models begin to trickle in. (On Tuesday, it announced a second wave of hardware : new iPad Pros, a MacBook Air, and Mac mini.)
In delivering a strong quarter with weakened guidance, Apple could alarm jittery tech investors after a month in which tech stocks took a drubbing.
In a conference call with analysts, Apple Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri pointed in part to uncertainty around supply and demand with a revamped hardware line for its guidance. Also on the call, Cook said exchange rates would have a negative impact of $2 billion on Apple’s revenue forecast for the fiscal first quarter.
At least one investor liked what he saw.
“We’re excited about the growth in the Services’ business, as we have for three years,” Trip Miller, managing partner at hedge fund Gullane Capital Partners, which owns an undisclosed number of Apple shares, tells Barron’s in a phone interview. “Apple has a tendency to be conservative in guidance, so that doesn’t concern me. Revenue is going up; just not as fast as some on Wall Street expected.”
Last week , Amazon.com (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOGL) reported earnings that handily beat analyst estimates but revenue that came up short, punishing both companies in after-hours trading. Shares of Netflix (NFLX) initially popped before tumbling. Newsletter Sign-up
Apple typically is the Teflon stock of tech, unimpeded by market conditions as it collects record revenue from iPhone and its booming Services business.
Apple reported fourth-quarter revenue of $11.4 billion in China , 18% of its total revenue. The region grew 16% year over year.
(Editor’s note: This article has been updated to include commentary from the conference call.)
